title: Backups
subtitle: Copies of all of {name} (boards, cards, comments, attachments, roles and teams) to download or restore whenever you want.
instanceSubtitle: Every account, organization, board and file of this instance in one file. Restoring one replaces EVERYTHING.
testOk: Connected: orgtable could write, read and delete a test file.
restored: Restored. A backup of what was there before is in the history.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.hint: Backups run at the chosen hour in the organization's time zone ({tz}).
schedule.retentionHint: Up to 90. The oldest scheduled ones are deleted; manual ones stay.
schedule.attachmentsHint: Without them the backup is much smaller, but files are not restored.
schedule.cronNote: Needs the hourly cron job POST /api/cron/backups (docs/backups.md).

destination.title: Where they are stored
destination.hint: Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.
destination.LOCALHint: Simple, but if the server is lost, they are lost with it.
destination.S3Hint: AWS, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO…
destination.keepKey: Leave it empty to keep the current one.
destination.encryptHint: AES-256; only an instance with this ORGTABLE_SECRET_KEY can open them.

history.title: History
history.restoreText: The organization's boards, teams and custom roles are replaced by the ones in this backup. A backup of what is there now is taken first. Type {confirm} to confirm.
history.restoreInstanceText: EVERYTHING in this instance (accounts, organizations, boards, files) is replaced by this backup, and everyone is signed out. A backup of what is there now is taken first. Type {confirm} to confirm.

export.title: Export
export.text: A .zip with readable JSON and the attachments, to take your data with you or open it in another orgtable instance.

import.title: Import
import.text: From an orgtable .zip. Its boards are added next to yours; people are matched by email among your members. A backup is taken first in case you need to go back.
import.tooLarge: The file is too large for this instance.
